newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two dead, two held in attack on army in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, two held in attack on army in Mexico.

text.p: Two gunmen were killed and two captured during a skirmish with a unit of the Mexican army in the southern state of Guerrero, the attorney general's office in the state capital said Monday.

In a statement, it said the fighting occured early Sunday in the village of Heliodoro Castillo, 60 miles northwest of the state capital Chilpancingo. But it denied it involved rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Army who have struck in several states since emerging in Guerrero in June.

Justice officials said the gunmen were not wearing EPR uniforms. A peasant leader from the region quoted witnesses as saying the shooting started when a drunk man fired a shotgun at an army helicopter patroling the region.
The chopper apparently shot back and killed him.

"Many other soldiers came on foot and it seems that when (the locals) heard the helicopter's machine gun they came out of their houses carrying shotguns and someone else was killed because the soldiers thought they were going to be attacked," said Severo Oyorzabal Diaz, head of a peasant organisation in the remote mountain region of Heliodoro Castillo.
He said army patrols had been stepped up in the region, where previously there had been no reports of EPR activity.

The attorney general's office said the two men in military custody were Joel Melquiades and Reynaldo Romero Arce, and that the two dead were Domingo Romero Arce, 21, and Rufino Landa Salgado, 24. Several AK-47 assault rifles were found at the scene, it added.
